summary: Backend-only offline review of the Lex 2.0 final legal-accuracy refinements. No paid LLM or Tavily calls were made, the frontend was not tested, and no data or app_settings were changed. Regression: all 19 requested suites pass when each is run on its own with AIA_NO_PAID=1 (21/36/34/44/21/16/4/34/91/45/12/13/12/5/8/5/43/18/12). The offline eval scores 117/117. build_review_pack, run to /tmp, gives A40/B16/C41/D38/E6/F8 = 149 items, each with a reviewer decision line, in both .md and .docx (6 tables). Its intro says nothing is professionally reviewed, and its output matches /app/memory/lex2_legal_review_pack.md exactly. The real DB does not have lex_ai_source_check enabled (read-only check). The new probe file tests/test_lex2_final_probe_iter55.py has 34 tests: 18 pass and 16 fail, and the 16 failures are 12 distinct defects. The most important: (1) the optional AI source check almost never places its qualifier correctly on real layer-1 output; (2) the new broader 'removed'/'removal'/'pregnan' patterns produce immigration, employment and emergency-detention false positives; (3) Scottish council PCN text applies the England & Wales 21-day postal rule.

critical.issue: In claim_support, the claim text is the sentence with the [n] markers removed but the full stop kept (e.g. 'Early conciliation usually lasts up to 8 weeks.'). run() then searches the answer for the first 60 characters of that text, but the answer still reads '...8 weeks [1].'. For any claim shorter than 60 characters, or where a marker falls in the first 60 characters, the anchor is not found. The check is still counted and charged (checked=1, est_gbp added), but no qualifier is added and the status is not updated. Reproduced through the real pipeline: finalize_answer -> run.

The insertion point is the LAST '.' on the line (out.rfind('.', m.start(), end_of_line)), not the end of the claim's own sentence. Example: 'Early conciliation ... 8 weeks before you can go on to claim [1]. Call Acas today.' becomes 'Call Acas (the cited source does not clearly support this...)', so the warning is attached to the wrong sentence.

minor.issue: A failed AI call is cached for 7 days as {'verdict':'uncertain','why':'check failed'}, so a temporary error stops that claim being retried for a week. est_gbp is also charged for failed calls.

The period check uses the whole sentence for each marker. 'Early conciliation lasts up to 6 weeks [1] and the time limit is 3 months less one day [2]' marks BOTH [1] and [2] as 'uncertain' and adds a false '**Source check:**' note, even though each source states its own period.

The number-word fallback is a plain substring test (_WORDN[d] in src), so 'two' inside 'network' or 'one' inside 'someone'/'done' counts as the period being found. A wrong period can therefore be marked source_supported.
min(2, len(terms)) is 0 when a sentence has no meaningful terms, so 'See this [1].' is recorded as source_supported. The checker also ignores 'fortnight' and '48 hours'.

The new '(?:will|to|going to) be removed' pattern catches non-immigration wording. 'I want my name to be removed from the joint tenancy' -> level high with immigration, and the Detention Duty Advice help line is added to the prompt. 'My employer said the tattoo has to be removed' -> immigration plus employment. 'The council says the car will be removed from outside my house' -> immigration, and 'emergency' (that level comes from the existing _DANGER match on 'outside my house'). Suggest requiring an immigration context word nearby (home office, deport, flight, centre, UK, country).

r'detain|removal|deport...' with no immigration context. Police detention ('arrested and detained at the police station') gets the immigration_core and emergency_detention rules in its prompt (high_stakes still correctly says criminal only). 'The removal company damaged my sofa' and 'removal of a director' also get both rules.
'pregnan\w*' with no workplace context: 'My wife is pregnant and our landlord served a section 21 notice' -> employment domain plus the et_time_limits rule in a housing question.

Scotland with served='post' skips the postal branch ('and not j.startswith("scot")') and falls into the 'service method not given' text. That text, for Scotland too, says 'if it was sent by post (camera/CCTV), the 21 days run from the date of service', which is the England & Wales postal rule. The lex_guidance Scotland rule says 14 days. Scotland should get one 14-day discount text, with a safe date.

The ALREADY PASSED flag is suppressed by any generic word: 'ago' ('you bought it 3 weeks ago'), 'ended' ('your employment ended'), 'expired' and so on. An answer that never says the deadline has passed still gets no flag. Suggest matching phrases about the deadline itself (e.g. '(deadline|time limit|date|period|discount)[^.]{0,40}(passed|expired|missed|ended)', 'out of time', 'too late').
Only 'D Month YYYY', 'DD/MM/YYYY' and 'D/M/YYYY' are recognised. If the answer gives the date as '5th January 2027' or 'January 5, 2027', a duplicate 'Dates worked out by the app' section is added.

Low impact: juris['deadline_items'] = auto_reminders is set before the hypothetical reset (auto_reminders = []), and juris['deadline_text'] is set before _dl_block += _HYPOTHETICAL_NOTE. For hypothetical questions, ensure_dates still adds dates labelled 'from the dates you gave'. Acceptable, but the label is inaccurate for hypotheticals.

action_items: source_ai_check.run: find the claim by matching against the answer with [n] markers removed (or store the original sentence or its offset in claim_support), and insert QUALIFIER at the end of that sentence (before its marker or full stop), not at the last '.' on the line.
source_ai_check: do not cache failed calls (or cache them only briefly) and do not add est_gbp for failures.

verify_citations: run the period check per marker on the clause before that marker, not the whole sentence. Make the _periods_in word fallback use word boundaries. Return False/None from _guidance_supported when no terms are found.

high_stakes immigration topic: limit '(will|to|going to) be removed' to immigration context. Tighten the lex_guidance emergency_detention regex so it excludes police detention and generic 'removal' (require immigration/home office/removal centre/deport/flight context).
Employment topic and et_time_limits: only match 'pregnan' with workplace context (employer, work, job, manager, hours, maternity leave).
deadline_calc._parking Scotland: one 14-day discount path for any service method (safe date notice+13), and never the 21-day England & Wales postal wording.
ensure_dates: narrow _PASSED_WORDS so generic 'ago'/'ended' no longer suppress the passed flag. Broaden _date_in to cover ordinal and 'Month D, YYYY' formats.
critical_code_review_comments: source_ai_check anchors on c['text'][:60], which comes from _NUM_MARK.sub('', sent) and so cannot match text that still has its markers. This is a design mismatch between layer 1 and layer 3 that the existing unit test hides, because it uses hand-written claim text with no full stop.
lex_guidance and high_stakes regexes are getting broader without negative examples. The probe file adds negative cases; consider adding them to the eval scenarios.
build_review_pack section titles hard-code their counts ('(40)', '(41)', '(38)'). Work them out from len(items) so the titles cannot drift from the data.

_HINT_RE is now much broader (bought, notice, contract, owe, removed, crash...). Combined with any digit or 'week' in the message, this sends more questions to the paid Haiku extraction call. The cost is small, but it is an increase in paid calls.

success_rate.backend: Regression 19/19 suites pass; offline eval 117/117; new probes 18/34 (16 failing tests = 12 distinct defects)

seed_data_creation: None. The review pack was rebuilt to /tmp only; /app/memory files were not overwritten. Real DB read-only check: lex_ai_source_check is not enabled.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run every suite on its own: AIA_NO_PAID=1 python -m pytest tests/<file>.py -q. Do not run test_lex_routing (it makes live paid calls). The probe file tests/test_lex2_final_probe_iter55.py documents the defects; once they are fixed it should pass in full. /tmp/pack_check.py shows how to rebuild the review pack to /tmp without overwriting /app/memory.
